offered_action_specs.name: rollback_deploy
offered_action_specs.description: Roll one service back to the settings it ran before its latest deploy, as the deploy log records them. Code plans it from that log, not from your tools' results, so you can name it even when they cannot see deploys: if the log holds no deploy of that service to undo, or the service changed since, code refuses it. Its container is recreated, so the service pauses while it restarts. Money already booked wrong stays wrong: a rollback stops new damage, and repairs nothing.

proposed.why: The logs confirm that webhook-receiver rejects every provider webhook for a bad signature, starting after its v2 secret deploy, and that explains why the books cannot catch up.

diagnosis.hypothesis: webhook-receiver was redeployed at 19:17:12 with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2. The provider still signs with the old secret, so the receiver refuses each webhook with 400 'signature mismatch'. Refused webhooks are never acknowledged and never reach Kafka. The provider keeps retrying them, so the backlog grows, the consumers never book these events, and the money check cannot settle to its cutoff (186 unacknowledged).

evidence.shows: All containers are running and healthy. webhook-receiver alone was recreated late, at 19:17:12.
The newest deploy is webhook-receiver at 19:17:12, 1.1 min before the check, changing WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION to v2. No other service changed.
Every recent POST to /webhooks/provider returns 400, each with a WARNING 'webhook refused: bad signature' (reason: signature mismatch), at a high rate, consistent with provider retries.
The empty WARN/ERROR search was a filter mismatch (the level is WARNING), not an absence of errors.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll webhook-receiver back to its previous settings (the prior WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION) so its signatures match the provider's again. The provider keeps retrying unacknowledged webhooks, so the backlog should drain on its own, and the consumers' idempotent and by-id handlers absorb any duplicates. Afterwards, run money_check with wait=true to confirm the books settle. Rotate to v2 only after the provider signs with the v2 secret, or accept both secrets during the change.

diagnosis.blast_radius: The webhook-receiver container is recreated, so webhook intake pauses for a few seconds. Webhooks sent during the pause go unacknowledged and the provider retries them, so nothing is lost. The surge of retried webhooks may briefly raise Kafka consumer lag. Two things remain unverified: whether the old secret is still the one the provider uses (only presumed), and whether the provider caps its retries. If it does, some events could be dropped for good and would need a replay or a data repair.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If signatures still fail after the rollback, redeploy webhook-receiver with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2 and coordinate the secret with the provider instead, ideally by having the receiver accept both versions during the rotation.
